source: Research for ultra.py, 2026-11-22. Searched for M5 Ultra and M3 Ultra Mac Studio results with wall power: Notebookcheck (processor and GPU pages, news), Tom's Hardware, Ars Technica, Gearlive, Macworld/Macwelt/Macworld Sweden, Tom's Guide, Japanese reviews, Jeff Geerling, the Julia Discourse GEMM thread, Blender Open Data. No source publishes a wall-power reading of either machine in a named benchmark, so every row here keeps an estimated power (est + pe).

nbc_m5u.name: Notebookcheck, Apple M5 Ultra processor benchmarks (Mac Studio Mac17,15, 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 256 GB)

gearlive_m5u.name: Gearlive, M5 Ultra Mac Studio review (M3 Ultra comparison figures)

cinebench2024.note: One entry in Notebookcheck's database for this unit; no Notebookcheck review text or wall power published.
One entry in Notebookcheck's database for this unit.

cpubench.note: Notebookcheck lists two runs on this configuration; their mean is used. Cross-check: Gearlive's own Geekbench 6 multi-core run on a 36-core, 256 GB unit was 37,870 (version not stated).
Notebookcheck lists two runs on this configuration; their mean is used.

Other reviews of the same configuration scored higher: Tom's Hardware 17,825 to 18,069 over ten runs (https://www.tomshardware.com/desktops/mini-pcs/apple-mac-studio-m5-ultra-review), Gearlive 17,960, Macworld Sweden 17,819 and Macwelt 16,934 (https://www.macworld.com/article/2973459/2026-mac-studio-m5-release-date-specs-price-rumors.html). Notebookcheck's run is used because it is the same unit as the Cinebench 2024 and Geekbench 6 rows.

cpubench.unit: M3 Ultra Mac Studio (configuration not stated)
cpubench.note: Gearlive gives 28,376 as the M3 Ultra's Geekbench 6 multi-core score beside its M5 Ultra run (37,870); the Geekbench 6 minor version and the M3 Ultra configuration are not stated.

not_found.item: M5 Ultra and M3 Ultra wall power in Cinebench, games or Blender
not_found.why: No review found publishes a wall reading in a named test. Apple's support page gives only idle and maximum (M5 Ultra 9 W / 385 W, M3 Ultra 9 W / 270 W). Ars Technica gives powermetrics chip power (about 75 W in HandBrake), not wall power; Notebookcheck's GPU page cites about 155 W GPU power in an MLX load; a Japanese review says only 'over 250 W under full load'.

not_found.item: M5 Ultra Cinebench 2026 single-core, M3 Ultra Geekbench 6 single-core and Cinebench 2026
not_found.why: Not published by any source found; Gearlive says only that its M5 Ultra Cinebench 2026 multi-core run was 47% ahead of the M3 Ultra, without the M3 Ultra score.

not_found.item: M5 Ultra and M3 Ultra Cyberpunk 2077 (1080p Ultra), Baldur's Gate 3 (1080p Ultra) and AC Shadows (1080p Ultra High)
not_found.why: Notebookcheck has no game results for either. Tom's Hardware and Gearlive ran Cyberpunk at 1080p with the Ray Tracing Ultra preset (66 fps) and Gearlive ran Baldur's Gate 3 at 4K Ultra (over 80 fps): other settings than this page's, and with no wall power, so the Cyberpunk model estimate stays and no BG3 or ACS point is added.

The Blender 4.5.0 medians on this page already come from the 2026-11-21 Open Data snapshot (one run each for the 30-core CPU and 64-core GPU); Notebookcheck's 80-core GPU figure (about 15,350) is from a later Blender version, which this page does not mix. Only the CPU rows' borrowed power changes here, following the new Cinebench 2024 row.

not_found.item: M5 Ultra HPL, M5 Ultra Julia GEMM, M3 Ultra Hubner et al. SGEMM
not_found.why: No HPL run published (Geerling has only the M3 Ultra); the Julia Discourse AppleNeuralEngine.jl thread has no M5 Ultra post as of 2026-11-22; Hubner et al. test base chips only.
